papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for spacecraft trajectory optimization with exact boundary conditions
papers.summary: We use neural networks to optimize trajectories by modeling the position as a function of time and minimizing the thrust with respect to the network parameters. This corresponds to an unsupervised training procedure in which physical laws are incorporated directly into the optimization objective. In standard physics-informed neural networks, initial and terminal states are enforced through additional weighted loss terms, resulting in a multi-objective optimization problem that is highly sensitive to the choice of loss weights and can lead to poor convergence and reduced accuracy. To address this challenge, we construct a simple transformation, exploiting the mathematical structure of trajectory optimization problems, to enforce boundary conditions exactly a-priori. This transformation can be interpreted as a reparameterization of the solution space that embeds the boundary conditions directly into the function. This converts the original constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one over admissible trajectories. I.e. the transformation eliminates the boundary condition penalty terms and reduces the problem to a single-objective optimization. Crucially, trajectory optimization comes with a low-dimensional boundary, which allows particularly simple and stable constructions of distance functions compared to general domains in partial differential equations. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach meaningfully improves convergence behavior and solution accuracy.
papers.title_ja: 厳密な境界条件を用いた宇宙機軌道最適化のための物理情報ニューラルネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、物理法則を最適化目標に組み込むことで宇宙機の軌道を最適化する物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）の手法を提案する。従来の手法では境界条件を損失関数の重み付き項として扱うため、重みの選択に敏感で収束性が悪くなる問題があった。本研究では、軌道最適化問題の数学的構造を利用した変換により、境界条件を事前かつ厳密に満たすように解空間を再パラメータ化し、制約付き問題を制約なしの単一目的最適化問題に変換する。このアプローチにより、収束挙動と解の精度が有意に向上することが数値実験で示された。

papers.title: A Neural Envelope Method for Rapid Gradient-based Optimum Takeoff Trajectory Design
papers.summary: Urban air mobility arises to mitigate ground traffic congestion. Multidisciplinary analysis and optimization (MDAO) has been introduced to reduce the energy consumption, thereby expanding aircraft performance. Surrogate-based MDAO lowers the cost of optimization, but multimodality disrupts global optimum search for both simulation-based and surrogate-based optimizations. Convex envelopes convert multimodal spaces into unimodal spaces, permitting efficient convex optimization; however, convexifying a design space may produce infeasible "optimal" designs due to complex design constraints. To address these challenges, this work proposes the coupling of a physics-constrained generative adversarial networks (physicsGAN) and neural envelope to transform original, constrained, non-convex optimizations into unconstrained, convex optimizations. Specifically, the physicsGAN discovers a feasible design space where all design candidates inherently satisfy all constraints, by penalizing surrogate-predicted constraint violations during training. Moreover, the neural envelope constructs a neural network-based convex envelope for the transformed objective function within the physicsGAN-discovered feasible space. Note that the neural envelope only needs to deal with objective function since constraints are inherently satisfied in the feasible space. The neural envelope is demonstrated on takeoff trajectory optimizations of the Airbus A3 Vahana eVTOL aircraft. Results show that neural envelopes achieve a 99.91% mean accuracy within a flight-condition space compared with reference convex envelopes. Neural-envelope-enabled optimizations achieve 99.84% accuracy on the global optimum design, costing only 0.04 seconds on average. The neural envelope accelerates the trajectory optimization by 53 and 162 times on average compared to the physicsGAN-enabled gradient-based and global optimizations, respectively.
papers.title_ja: 離陸軌道設計の高速勾配ベース最適化のためのニューラルエンベロープ法
papers.summary_ja: 都市航空機（eVTOL）の離陸軌道設計において、非凸な最適化問題を効率的に解く手法を提案する。物理制約付きGAN（physicsGAN）により制約条件を満たす実行可能領域を生成し、その中でニューラルネットワークを用いて目的関数の凸エンベロープを構築する。これにより、複雑な制約を扱うことなく凸最適化として解くことが可能になる。A3 Vahanaの事例では、参照解に対する精度99.84%を達成し、従来の手法比で最大162倍の高速化を実現した。

papers.title: Spatially local mini-batching for implicit neural representations
papers.summary: Neural surrogates based on implicit neural representations (INRs) are typically trained on mini-batches spread over the whole domain, since a generic INR loses accuracy when every point of a batch lies in one small region. We show that low-rank neural representations (LRNRs), INRs whose weight matrices are products of shared bases with coefficients emitted by a small hypernetwork, can be trained with spatially local mini-batches. Each step uses the points of one time snapshot of an adaptive-mesh numerical solution inside one small cell, with snapshots and cells drawn according to the refinement of the mesh. We posit that such training is enabled by the structural property of LRNRs, as a local step reaches the shared bases only through the $r$ coefficients of each layer, and keeps one cell from rewriting the network. By a Kolmogorov-width argument, we show that when restricted to a small cell, the hidden states of LRNRs lie close to a low-dimensional subspace, which suggests the local steps only affect low-rank subspaces of the shared bases. On six hyperbolic-conservation-law problems with solutions computed using adaptive mesh refinement, one local training recipe reaches 1.1-2.3% relative $L^2$ error with a tenth of the parameters of a dense network of the same width. Finally, we provide a comparison by training a hypernetwork-SIREN, a DeepONet, and a Fourier neural operator (FNO) of the same size with the same local batches and training budget. We observe that these baselines reach 16-78% where the LRNR reaches 4.9%. Interestingly, we also observe that local training has a significant effect on the per-cell low-dimensional structure even in a wide generic hypernetwork-SIREN.
papers.title_ja: 暗黙的ニューラル表現における空間的に局所的なミニバッチ学習
papers.summary_ja: 暗黙的ニューラル表現（INR）のサロゲートモデルにおいて、低ランク構造を持つLRNRが空間的に局所的なミニバッチで効率的に学習できることを示した。適応メッシュ解の小さなセル内のデータを用いた局所学習により、共有基底への影響を低次元部分空間に限定し、ネットワーク全体の劣化を防ぐメカニズムを理論的に説明した。双曲型保存則問題において、同幅の稠密ネットワークの1/10のパラメータ数で1.1〜2.3%の相対L2誤差を達成し、DeepONetやFNOなどの既存手法を大幅に上回る精度を示した。

papers.title: Efficient Robust Optimization via an Adaptive Mono-Level Gaussian Process Surrogate
papers.summary: Optimization under uncertainty seeks designs that perform robustly despite varying operating conditions or uncertain model parameters. However, identifying such designs typically requires solving an optimization problem with a nested uncertainty analysis, resulting in a high computational burden. Surrogate models can alleviate this burden and enable optimization under uncertainty even with computationally expensive simulation models. This paper proposes a novel surrogate-based approach that reduces the number of costly model evaluations required for robust optimization. The approach adopts a mono-level strategy, in which a single Gaussian process surrogate is constructed and adaptively refined for both optimization and uncertainty analysis. Refinement in the design space is guided by a sampling-based uncertainty indicator that propagates the surrogate's epistemic uncertainty to the robustness measure. Efficient uncertainty estimation is crucial for the scalability of the algorithm and achieved through pathwise sampling combined with a weight-space representation of the Gaussian process. The proposed approach is evaluated on several analytical benchmark models and requires fewer model evaluations than a state-of-the-art bi-level surrogate approach while achieving comparable solution accuracy. Once trained, the mono-level surrogate can be reused to optimize different robustness measures at reduced cost. Moreover, the approach is successfully applied to a structural optimization problem with constraints and design variable uncertainty.
papers.title_ja: 適応型単層ガウス過程サロゲートによる効率的な頑健最適化
papers.summary_ja: 不確実性下での最適化において、計算コストの高いネスト型不確実性解析を回避するため、単一のガウス過程サロゲートを最適化と不確実性解析の両方に適応的に活用する手法を提案する。設計空間の改善は、サロゲートの認識的不確実性を頑健性指標へ伝播させるサンプリングベースの不確実性指標によって導かれる。パスワイズサンプリングと重み空間表現を用いることで、アルゴリズムのスケーラビリティを確保しつつ、既存の二層型手法より少ないモデル評価回数で同等の精度を実現した。構造最適化問題への適用を通じて、訓練済みのサロゲートを再利用して異なる頑健性指標を低コストで最適化できることを示した。

papers.title: PANO: Parallel Latent Space Neural Operator for Solving PDEs
papers.summary: Aggregating observations into a limited number of latent tokens and learning physical interactions in the latent space has emerged as an effective approach for Transformer-based neural operators to solve Partial Differential Equation (PDE) problems involving large-scale observations. However, existing methods typically compress observations using a single aggregation pattern, making physical information not retained by that pattern invisible to the latent space and thereby constraining physical interactions within it. To address this limitation, we propose PArallel Latent Space Neural Operator (PANO), a novel neural operator for solving PDEs that formulates physical interactions among observations as an additive combination of interaction results from parallel latent spaces with shared parameters. Specifically, PANO transforms observations into multiple distinct compressed representations through independent mappings, learns physical interactions in parallel based on these representations, and finally fuses the decoded results to predict the target physical field. Within PANO, we further propose Coupled Assignment Projection (CAP) to construct bidirectionally consistent encoding and decoding mappings, and Pairwise Latent Space Attention Layer (PaLA) to jointly update latent representations of each latent space through adaptive cross-space interactions. Extensive experiments on nine benchmarks spanning diverse physical systems, geometries, and observation scales demonstrate that PANO achieves state-of-the-art performance. Notably, PANO reduces equivalent plastic strain prediction errors on Unilateral Stamping by 28.3% (or more) and lift-coefficient prediction errors on AirCraft by 21.4% (or more) compared with existing methods. Code is available at https://github.com/ZijiangY1116/PANO.
papers.title_ja: PANO: 偏微分方程式の解法における並列潜在空間ニューラルオペレータ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、Transformerベースのニューラルオペレータにおける単一集約パターンによる情報損失を解決するため、並列潜在空間で物理的相互作用を学習するPANOを提案する。観測データを複数の独立した圧縮表現に変換し、それらの相互作用結果を加法結合することで、より正確な物理場の予測を実現する。さらに、双方向に整合したエンコード/デコードマッピングを構築するCAPと、適応的なクロススペース相互作用を通じて潜在表現を共同更新するPaLAを導入した。9つのベンチマーク実験において、既存手法と比較して最大28.3%の予測誤差低減など、最先端の性能を達成したことを示している。

papers.title: High-Dimensional Black-Box Optimization via Guidance Sampling of Diffusion Models
papers.summary: Many real-world optimization problems involve optimizing black-box objectives for which only a limited number of evaluations are available. Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful framework for such problems, but its effectiveness often deteriorates in high-dimensional spaces. Recent work leverages diffusion models for black-box optimization, often through pre-training a reward-conditioned score network to steer generation towards high-reward samples. Alternatively, gradient-based guidance methods assume access to a differentiable reward function from which guidance gradients are queried. However, these approaches either require large amounts of labeled data for offline training or access to exact reward gradients, limiting their applicability in black-box settings. We propose BReaD (Black-box Reward-guided Sampling of Diffusion Model), a guidance sampling framework for optimizing black-box rewards without assuming access to a labeled dataset or reward gradients. The proposed method uses a Gaussian process (GP) as a differentiable surrogate for the unknown objective and actively queries labels for the generated samples. We provide a theoretical analysis of the total-variation distance between the generated distribution and the target distribution. Using Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) as guidance signals, our method balances exploration and exploitation during generation and enables the discovery of high-reward regions in the data space. Numerical experiments on scientific discovery and image generation tasks demonstrate that our framework can effectively optimize black-box rewards in low-data scenarios.
papers.title_ja: 拡散モデルのガイダンスサンプリングによる高次元ブラックボックス最適化
papers.summary_ja: 高次元空間におけるブラックボックス最適化問題を解決するため、拡散モデルとガウス過程（GP）を組み合わせる手法BReaDを提案する。ラベル付きデータセットや報酬関数の勾配に依存せず、GPを微分可能なサロゲートモデルとして用いることで、生成サンプルに対して能動的にラベルをクエリする。UCB（Upper Confidence Bound）をガイダンスシグナルとして活用し、探索と活用のバランスを取りながら高報酬領域を発見する。科学発見や画像生成タスクにおける数値実験により、低データ環境下での有効性を示した。

papers.title: OpenPINN/PINO: An Extensible Open-Source Framework for Agent-Assisted Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Neural Operators
papers.summary: Substantial challenges in physics-informed learning have motivated many improvements, but fragmented implementations hinder systematic organization, integration, and comparison. We propose OpenPINN/PINO, an extensible open-source PyTorch framework for physics-informed neural networks and neural operators. Two shared specifications connect problem setup, local computation, and evaluation. Agents support problem formulation, solver planning, and diagnosis. ProblemSpec defines geometry, governing equations, constitutive relations, parameters, initial and boundary conditions, and optional data. MethodSpec configures the model, sampling, loss, optimization, and differentiation. Researchers can register new problem templates and method components, then combine or compare strategies such as Fourier features, residual-adaptive sampling, and self-adaptive loss weighting for a fixed problem. Agents translate natural-language descriptions into specifications, flag missing information, and propose solver plans. The framework validates these specifications and deterministically generates local training and testing code. A diagnostic agent reviews training logs and evaluation results to identify problems and suggest revisions. Three examples show how method choices and agent diagnostics affect accuracy. For viscous Burgers, Fourier features and residual-adaptive sampling each reduced relative $L^2$ error by about $75\%$ from a shared baseline. For periodic Poisson, spectral differentiation reduced mean-free relative $L^2$ error by about $68\%$ across 16 held-out forcings. For a plate with a hole, successive agent diagnoses guided nondimensionalization and optimization. After initial training failure, all three runs met the $10\%$ target, with relative $L^2$ displacement errors of $3.51\%$--$6.31\%$.
papers.title_ja: OpenPINN/PINO: エージェント支援による物理情報ニューラルネットとニューラルオペレータのための拡張可能なオープンソースフレームワーク

papers.title: Structure and asymptotic preserving deep neural surrogates for uncertainty quantification in multiscale kinetic equations
papers.summary: The high dimensionality of kinetic equations with stochastic parameters poses major computational challenges for uncertainty quantification (UQ). Traditional Monte Carlo (MC) sampling methods, while widely used, suffer from slow convergence and high variance, which become increasingly severe as the dimensionality of the parameter space grows. To accelerate MC sampling, we adopt a multiscale control variates strategy that leverages low-fidelity solutions from simplified kinetic models to reduce variance. To further improve sampling efficiency and preserve the underlying physics, we introduce surrogate models based on structure and asymptotic preserving neural networks (SAPNNs). These deep neural networks are specifically designed to satisfy key physical properties, including positivity, conservation laws, entropy dissipation, and asymptotic limits. By training the SAPNNs on low-fidelity models and enriching them with selected high-fidelity samples from the full Boltzmann equation, our method achieves significant variance reduction while maintaining physical consistency and asymptotic accuracy. The proposed methodology enables efficient large-scale prediction in kinetic UQ and is validated across both homogeneous and nonhomogeneous multiscale regimes. Numerical results demonstrate improved accuracy and computational efficiency compared to standard MC techniques.
papers.title_ja: 多スケール運動論方程式の不確実性定量化における構造と漸近保存深層ニューラルサロゲート
papers.summary_ja: 確率的パラメータを持つ高次元運動論方程式の不確実性定量化（UQ）において、モンテカルロ法の変動を低忠実度モデルを用いた制御変数戦略で低減する手法を提案する。さらに、正性・保存則・エントロピー散逸などの物理的性質と漸近極限を厳密に満たす構造と漸近保存ニューラルネットワーク（SAPNN）をサロゲートモデルとして導入する。低忠実度モデルで訓練し、ボルツマン方程式の高忠実度サンプルで補強することで、物理的一貫性と計算効率を両立させる。均質・非均質の多スケール領域で検証され、標準的なモンテカルロ法より精度と効率の向上を示した。

papers.title: Micro-Macro Tensor Neural Surrogates for Uncertainty Quantification in Collisional Plasma
papers.summary: Plasma kinetic equations exhibit pronounced sensitivity to microscopic perturbations in model parameters and data, making reliable and efficient uncertainty quantification (UQ) essential for predictive simulations. However, the cost of uncertainty sampling, the high-dimensional phase space, and multiscale stiffness pose severe challenges to both computational efficiency and error control in traditional numerical methods. These aspects are further emphasized in presence of collisions where the high-dimensional nonlocal collision integrations and conservation properties pose severe constraints. To overcome this, we present a variance-reduced Monte Carlo framework for UQ in the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau (VPL) system, in which neural network surrogates replace the multiple costly evaluations of the Landau collision term. The method couples a high-fidelity, asymptotic-preserving VPL solver with inexpensive, strongly correlated surrogates based on the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Euler--Poisson (EP) equations. For the surrogate models, we introduce a generalization of the separable physics-informed neural network (SPINN), developing a class of tensor neural networks based on an anisotropic micro-macro decomposition, to reduce velocity-moment costs, model complexity, and the curse of dimensionality. To further increase correlation with VPL, we calibrate the VPFP model and design an asymptotic-preserving SPINN whose small- and large-Knudsen limits recover the EP and VP systems, respectively. Numerical experiments show substantial variance reduction over standard Monte Carlo, accurate statistics with far fewer high-fidelity samples, and lower wall-clock time, while maintaining robustness to stochastic dimension.
papers.title_ja: 衝突プラズマにおける不確実性定量化のためのミクロ・マクロテンソルニューラルサロゲート
papers.summary_ja: 衝突プラズマのVlasov-Poisson-Landau系における不確実性定量化（UQ）を高速化するため、Landau衝突項の評価をニューラルネットワークサロゲートに置き換える分散低減モンテカルロ枠組みを提案する。速度モーメントコストと次元の呪いを低減するため、異方性ミクロ・マクロ分解に基づくテンソルニューラルネットワークを設計し、物理情報ニューラルネット（PINN）の一般化として適用した。高忠実度ソルバーと低コストサロゲートを結合することで、標準モンテカルロ法よりも大幅に少ないサンプル数で統計量を高精度に推定し、計算時間を短縮しつつ頑健性を維持することを数値実験で示した。

papers.title: KVUse: Reusable-KV User Memory for Efficient LLM Recommenders
papers.summary: Memory-augmented recommenders built on large language models (LLMs) maintain a natural-language profile of each user. These profiles are updated by a user profile update path that revises the profile as new interactions arrive and are consumed by downstream task paths like ranking. Because these user profiles are stored as text in the user memory, every ranking LLM call that consumes them must splice them in the prompt and calculate the KV cache of them during the prefill phase. Given these ranking LLM calls are prefill heavy (long prompt but short decoded output) and repeatedly called, these repeated prefill of user profile text dominates the serving. Prefix caching cannot remove it, because these user profiles are preceded by different text in different calls. We present KVUse, which stores the user profiles as reusable key-value (KV) caches instead of text. KVUse trains lightweight LoRA writers by self-distillation, so that the user profile update call produces the reusable KV of the user profile while decoding it, and the LLM can read these reusable KV at new positions and behind new context without recomputation. KVUse also has a customized KV scheduler that uploads the stored reusable KV of the next batch while the current batch is computed, hiding the KV transfer from host memory behind GPU computation. On four InstructRec datasets with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, KVUse shows no statistically significant difference in ranking quality from full prefill over continuous memory update rounds. Under saturated load, KVUse raises the throughput of the downstream scoring path by 4.0x-4.5x and of the profile update path by 1.4x-1.9x.
papers.title_ja: KVUse: 効率的なLLMレコメンダーのための再利用可能なKVユーザーメモリ
papers.summary_ja: LLMベースのレコメンダーにおいて、ユーザープロファイルのテキストを毎回プリフィルで計算するコストを削減する手法を提案する。ユーザープロファイルのキーバリュー（KV）キャッシュを再利用可能に保存し、LoRAによる自己蒸留で生成・読み出しを行うことで、再計算を回避する。さらに、KVスケジューラによりGPU計算中にKV転送を隠蔽し、スループットを向上させる。実験では、ランキング品質を維持しつつ、スコアリングパスのスループットを最大4.5倍に改善した。

papers.title: Unveiling the mutual inclination distribution in astrometric surveys
papers.summary: Mutual inclination in three (or more) body systems (triple stars, circumbinary planets, multi-planetary systems, etc.) is a tracer of their formation and evolution. Gaia Data Release 4 will provide for the first time a catalog of orbital solutions for three-body systems. Because astrometry is only sensitive to the motion in the plane of the sky, there is a degeneracy in the orbital solutions leading to two possible solutions for the mutual inclination in three-body systems. We propose a hierarchical Bayesian framework to circumvent this degeneracy and unveil the mutual inclination distribution in the population. We tested our methods on simulated datasets, and showed that it reliably recovered the injected mutual inclination distributions in various cases. The method is thus promising for the statistical analysis of Gaia DR4 three-body systems.
papers.title_ja: 天測調査における相互傾斜分布の解明
papers.summary_ja: 三重星や周回二重星惑星などの三体系における相互傾斜は、形成と進化の指標となる。Gaia DR4では天測データによる軌道解の縮退（2つの解）が生じる問題に対し、階層的ベイズフレームワークを提案した。シミュレーションデータを用いた検証により、注入された相互傾斜分布を信頼性高く復元できることを示した。この手法はGaia DR4の三体系統計解析に有望である。
